subjects.label: The roster: mains, menaces and missing fighters
subjects.description: Named fighters on the roster: the one a player mains or adores, the ones that are miserable to fight against, and the fighter who is missing and should be added; not the cast as figures in the story.

subjects.label: Ranks and the ranked ladder
subjects.description: The ranked ladder: the rank colour reached and the climb to it, leaver penalties, opponents who leave after one match, veterans lurking in the low ranks; not connection quality or the fighting system itself.

subjects.label: Disconnects, ping and regions
subjects.description: Staying connected to an opponent: matches dropping, unstable ping, lag switchers, and which region you are matched into and how it is decided; not the ranked ladder or the community's manners.

subjects.label: Offence over defence: heat, mashing and guesses
subjects.description: The fighting system's tilt towards attack: the heat mechanic and its drives, rage arts and throws, mashing and one-move gameplans, the loss of sidestep and mind games, and rounds decided by a guess in seconds; not patches or specific fighters.

subjects.label: Seasons and balance patches
subjects.description: The seasonal patches and what they did: a season launching or disappointing, nerfs to named fighters, and calls to revert or hotfix a patch; not the studio's general conduct or the fighting system's design.

subjects.label: The producers and publisher by name
subjects.description: Reviews that address the game's producers or its publisher by name or nickname, to thank them, blame them or tell them to retire; not complaints about patches that name nobody.

subjects.label: Tilt, rage and blood pressure
subjects.description: What losing does to the player: the game as a hazard to sanity, raised blood pressure, humiliation and the burning pain of being juggled, told as a joke or a warning; not the mood or immersion of the game itself.

subjects.label: Getting good: the skill gap and the climb
subjects.description: A player's own skill: learning to block lows and read the opponent, feeling hopeless, veterans stomping newcomers, simplified inputs as a crutch, and the courage to keep practising; not the tutorial or the modes that teach.

subjects.label: Fighter bodies, hair and costumes
subjects.description: How the fighters look and dress: body physics, a changed hairstyle, the physiques on offer, and the costumes and customisation items; not the stages, effects or overall art style.

subjects.label: Pros, streamers and tournaments
subjects.description: The game as something watched: pro players and streamers by name or handle, coming to the game from YouTube, and how tournaments are run; not the ordinary playerbase's manners.

subjects.label: Against the earlier entries and the next one
subjects.description: This entry set against its numbered predecessors, playing since an older entry, and praying for the next number; not comparisons to other games or genres.
